'''''Fermat's Last Theorem''''' is a [[popular science]] book (1997) by [[Simon Singh]]. It tells the story of the search for a proof of [[Fermat's Last Theorem]], first conjectured by [[Pierre de Fermat]] in 1637, and explores how many mathematicians such as [[Évariste Galois]] had tried and failed to provide a proof for the theorem.<ref name="mr">Review of ''Fermat's Enigma'' by Andrew Bremner (1998), {{MR|1491363}}.</ref><ref name="Guardian">{{citation|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2013/aug/02/fermats-last-theorem-simon-singh-review|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|title=Fermat's Last Theorem by Simon Singh – book review. A boast in the margin of a book is the starting point for a wonderful journey through the history of mathematics, number theory and logic|first=Tim|last=Radford|date=2 August 2013}}.</ref><ref name="nyt">{{citation|url=https://www.nytimes.com/books/97/11/30/reviews/971130.30penrost.html|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|first=Roger|last=Penrose|authorlink=Roger Penrose|date=November 30, 1997|title=Q.E.D. How to solve the greatest mathematical puzzle of your age: Lock self in room. Emerge seven years later}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url= http://canadaam.ctvnews.ca/math-problem-a-300-year-saga-of-death-duels-dual-identities-1.2822673| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160318135455/http://canadaam.ctvnews.ca/math-problem-a-300-year-saga-of-death-duels-dual-identities-1.2822673| url-status= dead| archive-date= March 18, 2016| title= Math problem a 300-year saga of death, duels, dual identities| last=Elliott| first=Josh| work=[[CTV News]]| date= 18 March 2016| accessdate=31 July 2016}}</ref> Despite the efforts of many mathematicians, the proof would remain incomplete until 1995, with the publication of [[Andrew Wiles]]' [[Wiles' proof of Fermat's Last Theorem|proof of the Theorem]]. The book is the first mathematics book to become a Number One seller in the United Kingdom,<ref>{{cite news|url= https://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/2016/03/20/why-its-so-impressive-that-fermats-last-theorum-has-been-solved/| title= Why it's so impressive that Fermat's Last Theorem has been solved| last=Singh| first=Simon| work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]| date=24 May 2016| accessdate=31 July 2016}}</ref> whilst Singh's documentary ''The Proof'', on which the book was based, won a [[BAFTA]] in 1997.<ref>{{cite news|url= http://www.cs.uleth.ca/~kaminski/esferm03.html| title= The extraordinary story of Fermat's Last Theorem| work=[[University of Lethbridge]]| date=3 May 1997| accessdate=31 July 2016}}</ref>

In the United States, the book was released as ''Fermat's Enigma: The Epic Quest to Solve the World's Greatest Mathematical Problem''.<ref name="mr"/><ref name="nyt"/> The book was released in the United States in October 1998 to coincide with the US release of Singh's documentary ''The Proof'' about [[Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem]].<ref name="Guardian"/><ref name="AMS">{{cite web| url= https://www.ams.org/notices/199710/comm-fermat.pdf| title= Fermat's Enigma| last=Jackson| first=Allyn| publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]| date=October 1997| accessdate=31 July 2016}}</ref>
